subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
unit: Unit 5: A Letter to a Teacher (Writing)
lesson: Checking and editing a partner’s letter; writing the second draft
outcomes: Check a partner's letter for meaning and language with a checklist
Give helpful feedback and write a second draft

tf.s: You check meaning and content first in a partner's letter.
tf.why: Part 1 of the checklist is about meaning.

tf.s: You underline unclear ideas in pen.
A second draft is a new letter on a different topic.
tf.why: It is the same letter, corrected and improved.

tf.s: You should attach the first draft to the second draft.
tf.why: The teacher can see your changes.

tf.s: You must accept every comment your partner gives.
tf.why: You decide which comments are useful.

tf.s: The final draft goes into the portfolio with earlier drafts.
The editing checklist has a Language section.
Another reader can notice mistakes you missed.
tf.why: Fresh eyes see things you don't.

tf.s: Feedback should be rude so that it is remembered.
tf.why: Good feedback is polite and helpful.

tf.s: A second draft is a corrected and improved copy of the first draft.
tf.why: It includes the changes from feedback.

boxes.q: What do you use to underline unclear ideas?
What does Part 1 of the checklist check?
Where does the final draft go?
boxes.why: It is kept with earlier drafts.

boxes.q: What does the second draft include?
boxes.why: Only the errors and changes are added.

boxes.q: Why have someone else read your writing?
Which phrases can you use when giving feedback?

o: You should add a comma after 'First'.
boxes.why: Helpful comments are clear and specific.

boxes.q: What should you do with comments that are not useful?
How many questions are in the Language section?
What do you write after peer editing?
boxes.why: You use the feedback to improve your letter.

hunt.q: Attach this to your second draft
What to do with useless comments

mcq.q: What do you check first in a partner's letter?
What do you do with ideas you don't understand?
mcq.why: Your partner can then make them clearer.

o: The final draft with earlier drafts
mcq.why: The portfolio keeps all your drafts.

mcq.q: Which part of the checklist has questions 1–7?
mcq.why: The Language section checks grammar, spelling and punctuation.

mcq.q: Your partner wrote: 'First we went to the beach.' Which feedback is useful?
o: You should add a comma after 'First'.
mcq.why: Specific advice helps your partner improve.

mcq.q: Your partner's letter says 'I love my fammily.' What comment do you give?
You got five comments, but one would change your meaning wrongly. What do you do?
o: Disregard that comment and use the useful ones
mcq.why: Keep only the advice that helps.

mcq.q: Why should you accept some comments and disregard others?
o: Not all advice is useful, so you decide what to keep
mcq.why: You are the writer and make the final choice.

mcq.q: Why is the second draft not a whole new letter?
o: It improves the first draft using the feedback
mcq.why: Editing builds on your first work.

mcq.q: Why keep earlier drafts in your portfolio?
o: To show how your writing improved
